indexes.//: Published reviews, newest first. Default sort on the Reviews & Ratings page and the two-review preview on the nature detail page. A COLLECTION_GROUP index keyed on the `reviews` collection id, so it serves tours/*/reviews as well as nature_spots/*/reviews — Firestore indexes by collection id, not by path, so the tour ratings added in Phase 6 needed no new index at all.

Reviews & Ratings, 'Highest rated' sort. Ordered in the QUERY rather than in Dart on purpose: the list is paginated, so sorting a downloaded page would rank the newest 10 reviews and call them the highest rated of 128.
Reviews & Ratings, 'Lowest rated' sort. Same reasoning as above.

Reviews & Ratings, 'Most helpful' sort — the heart count the reference draws on every row. helpfulCount is server-owned (written only by the votes trigger), so this ordering cannot be gamed from a client.

Home screen carousel: featured.where('active', ==, true).orderBy('order'). An equality filter combined with an orderBy on a different field needs a composite index; Firestore's single-field indexes are not enough.
Explore Nature carousel: nature_spots.where('active', ==, true).where('highlighted', ==, true).orderBy('highlightOrder').

Explore Nature list: nature_spots.where('active', ==, true).orderBy('reviewScore', desc). This is the ONLY list query — every filter (quick chips, place types, facilities) is applied in Dart, because Firestore permits one array clause per query and the screen has three multi-select groups. No array-contains index is needed as a result.
Explore Tours carousel: tours.where('active', ==, true).where('highlighted', ==, true).orderBy('highlightOrder').

Explore Tours list: tours.where('active', ==, true).orderBy('startAt'). This is the ONLY list query. The search box cannot be a query at all — Firestore has no substring match, and the tour name is a locale map, so a server-side search would have to pick one of three languages. The date filter and the trending ordering are applied in Dart over the same read, so neither needs an index of its own.

My Bookings: bookings.where('userId', ==, uid).orderBy('startAt', desc). This is the ONLY bookings query — the type chips and the Upcoming/Past/Cancelled segment are both applied in Dart, because a composite index per combination would be five more indexes for a list that is small per user. See DATA_MODEL.md.
